images.title: Base and exponent in 5⁴
images.purpose: Names the base 5 and the exponent 4 in 5⁴ and shows it means four 5s multiplied, which is 625.
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. A large power 5⁴ on the left with two pointer labels, an expanded product in the middle and the value on the right, all on one horizontal line.
images.exact_structure: On the left, a large '5⁴': the 5 in teal (#0072B2), the raised small 4 in amber (#E69F00). A thin teal (#0072B2) pointer line from below the 5 leads to the label 'base'; a thin amber (#E69F00) pointer line from above the 4 leads to the label 'exponent'. To the right, an equals sign, then '5 × 5 × 5 × 5' with each of the four 5s in teal (#0072B2); a thin amber (#E69F00) brace under the four 5s. Then another equals sign and the value '625' inside a reddish purple (#CC79A7) rounded box. Exactly four 5s in the product, 1 brace, 2 pointers, 1 box.

images.takeaway: The exponent counts the equal factors: 5⁴ = 625.
images.description: Names the base 5 and the exponent 4 in 5⁴ and shows it means four 5s multiplied, which is 625.
images.context: 5⁴ = 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 625, not 5 × 4 = 20. The folding thickness after n folds is 0.001 × 2 to the power n cm.
images.teaching_notes: The equals sign appears twice. Point at the brace and count four factors to match the small 4.

image_decisions.why: Naming the base and exponent and expanding 5⁴ into four factors is the concept itself.
